gaps.sentence: Who ___ this bag belong to? It has been sitting here all morning.
gaps.hint: the question form needs auxiliary does
gaps.explanation: Present simple questions need the auxiliary 'does' plus the base verb: does this bag belong to.

gaps.sentence: She has bought the paint, so tomorrow she ___ the kitchen.
gaps.hint: an intention already decided before speaking
gaps.explanation: An intention decided before the moment of speaking uses 'be going to': is going to paint.

gaps.sentence: Every morning she ___ an hour in the garden before breakfast.
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' marks a repeated routine, which takes the present simple: spends.

gaps.hint: on the point of happening now
gaps.explanation: 'Be about to' expresses something on the point of happening: is about to start.

gaps.sentence: The phone is ringing. Don't worry, I ___ it.
gaps.hint: a spontaneous decision at the moment
gaps.explanation: Decisions made at the moment of speaking use 'will': will answer.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time she ___ a car on her own.
gaps.hint: it was the first time takes past perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It was the first time' in past contexts, English uses the past perfect: had driven.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: The wedding guests ___ when the string quartet began to play.
gaps.hint: in progress when the music began
gaps.explanation: An action in progress when a past event occurred takes the past continuous: were still arriving.
